title.en: Determining whether EMR procedures should be taken over by the supervising practitioner

statement.en: ESGE recommends the criteria listed below should be considered when determining when/if trainee EMR procedures should be taken over by their supervising practitioner.

text.en: Trainee is unable to carry out the instructions of the trainer despite comprehending them.
Lack of adequate progress due to any reason relevant to the level of training or competency.
Patient withdraws consent for a training procedure to be performed.
Patient is in significant discomfort and this is thought to be due to the involvement of a trainee.

Suspicion of area(s) of SMI within the lesion for EMR, which are deemed not to have been sufficiently/adequately interrogated prior to the EMR or by the trainee, and/or where a precise en bloc resection is required that may not be achievable by the trainee.
Unstable colonoscope position, with the trainee not able to maintain the optimal position on the lesion for snare placement (5–6 o’clock) despite input from the trainer.
Trainee unable to obtain adequate submucosal lift.
Trainee repeatedly cold snares the target lesion or resections lead only to superficial scraping of polyp tissue and incomplete excision of the mucosal layer.
Severe intraprocedural bleeding if the trainee is not competent/able to address this.
Perforation if the trainee is not competent/able to address this.
Trainee requests that the supervisor takes over the procedure.
Time constraints – when the endoscopy procedure, program, or unit is running significantly behind schedule, and the training episode is likely to be contributing to this.
